title: Outputs, outcomes, benefits and dis-benefits
blurb: Define output, capability, outcome, benefit, dis-benefit and business objective, and place any example on the chain that links them.
question: A project delivers a new online booking system, customers start booking online, and call-centre costs fall by 20%. Which of these is the output, which the outcome and which the benefit?

teach.body: Formally: projects deliver outputs (products). The completed set of outputs needed to deliver an outcome is a capability; putting the capability to use brings about change that leads to outcomes, and outcomes allow the organization to realize the benefits described in the business case, which contribute to business objectives. In plain English: the project builds the thing; people use the thing differently; the organization measures the improvement; the improvement moves the strategy forward.

teach.h: The chain from product to strategy

steps.label: Capability
steps.sub: the complete set of outputs needed

steps.label: Outcome
steps.sub: the result of change in behaviour

teach.caption: An outcome seen as negative by the investing organization leads to a dis-benefit: a measurable decline.

teach.body: An output is the tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity: a product. A capability is the completed set of project outputs required to deliver an outcome. An outcome is the result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour and circumstances; changes are implemented to achieve outcomes. Projects deliver outputs, so outcomes and most benefits arrive later, once the outputs are in use.

A benefit is the measurable improvement resulting from an outcome, perceived as an advantage by the investing organization, contributing to one or more business objectives. A dis-benefit is the measurable decline resulting from an outcome perceived as negative, detracting from those objectives. A business objective is a measurable outcome that shows progress against the organization's strategy, and the project should contribute to it.

teach.h: Six terms with one worked example
head: Term
Key words
E-prescribing example

teach.h: Telling the three main terms apart

teach.body: Marlow Bay Hospitals Trust's strategy includes a patient-safety business objective. Project manager Daniel Osei's project delivers e-prescribing software, handheld devices and training (outputs); together they form the capability. Once live, doctors prescribe electronically and pharmacists see orders at once (outcome). The business case forecasts 30% fewer prescribing errors (benefit) and records that ward rounds will take about five minutes longer per patient at first (dis-benefit), which senior user Dr Ines Moreau will monitor.

teach.text: Classic trap: calling an outcome a benefit, or an output an outcome. 'A new training course' is an output; 'staff now use the new procedure' is an outcome; '20% fewer complaints' is a benefit. Second trap: an outcome is not a quality expectation or an acceptance criterion; those describe the products, not the change.

items: Output: the tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity (a product).
Capability: the completed set of outputs needed to deliver an outcome.
Outcome: the result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour.
Benefit / dis-benefit: measurable improvement / decline from an outcome.
Business objective: measurable outcomes showing progress against strategy.
Chain: outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits, business objectives.

summary: You can now define output, capability, outcome, benefit, dis-benefit and business objective. You can also place any statement on the chain from product to strategy and spot when an outcome is being mislabelled as a benefit or an output.

options: The tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity
The result of change affecting real-world behaviour
A measurable improvement perceived as an advantage
The completed set of products needed for an outcome
A.why: An output is the tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity: a product (manual 5.1).

A.q: Which term describes a measurable decline resulting from an outcome perceived as negative by the investing organization?
options: Risk
Issue
Dis-benefit
Off-specification
A.why: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline resulting from an outcome perceived as negative, detracting from business objectives (manual 5.1).

whyNot.0: A risk is an uncertain event; a dis-benefit is a measured decline from an outcome.
whyNot.1: An issue is an event needing project management consideration.
whyNot.3: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications, a type of issue.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. An [?] is the result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour and circumstances.
options: outcome
output
objective
issue
A.why: An outcome is the result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour and circumstances (manual 5.1).

whyNot.1: An output is the deliverable of an activity, not the change it causes.
whyNot.2: A business objective is a measurable outcome that shows progress against strategy, not any result of change.
whyNot.3: An issue is an event that needs project management consideration.

B.q: A council project launches an online parking permit portal. After launch, residents apply online instead of by post. What is 'residents apply online instead of by post'?
options: An output
An outcome
A benefit
A capability
B.why: A change in how people behave is an outcome: the result of change in real-world behaviour.

whyNot.0: The output is the portal itself, the product.
whyNot.2: A benefit would be a measurable improvement, such as lower processing cost.
whyNot.3: The capability is the complete set of outputs (portal, guidance, trained staff) that enables the outcome.

B.q: For the same parking permit project, which is an example of a benefit?
options: The online portal goes live in March
Residents now apply online, not by post
The portal, help pages and training exist
Permit processing costs fall by 25%
B.why: A benefit is a measurable improvement resulting from an outcome; a 25% cost reduction is measurable.

whyNot.0: Launching the portal is delivering an output.
whyNot.1: This is the outcome: changed behaviour.
whyNot.2: This is the capability: the completed set of outputs.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. A business objective is an output the project must deliver.
2. Projects deliver outputs; most benefits are realized after the project.
3. A benefit contributes towards one or more business objectives.
4. An outcome is the tangible deliverable of an activity.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 3
1 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Projects deliver outputs and most benefits follow later (2); benefits contribute to business objectives (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is false: a business objective relates to strategy; the project contributes to it.
whyNot.2: Both are false: objectives are not outputs, and an outcome is not a deliverable.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: that is the definition of an output.

C.q: Which sequence correctly shows how a project contributes to an organization's strategy?
options: Outcomes, outputs, capabilities, benefits, business objectives
Outputs, outcomes, capabilities, business objectives, benefits
Outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits, business objectives
Capabilities, outputs, benefits, outcomes, business objectives
C.why: Outputs form capabilities, which lead to outcomes, which allow benefits to be realized, contributing to business objectives (manual 5.1, fig 5.1).

whyNot.0: Outcomes cannot come before the outputs that cause them.
whyNot.1: Capabilities are built from outputs before outcomes, and benefits feed objectives.
whyNot.3: Outputs come first, and benefits result from outcomes, not the reverse.

C.q: A rail operator's strategy targets 15% fewer delays by 2030. A project installs new signalling software. Which pairing is correct?
options: The software is an outcome; fewer delays is an output
The software is a capability; fewer delays is a risk
The software is a benefit; fewer delays is an outcome
The software is an output; the target is an objective
C.why: The software is a deliverable (output); a measurable strategic target is a business objective that the project contributes to.

whyNot.0: Software is a deliverable, not a change in behaviour, and a target is not an output.
whyNot.1: A strategic target is not a risk; a risk is an uncertain event.
whyNot.2: Software is not a measurable improvement; it is the product.

C.q: After a hotel launches self-service check-in, front-desk staff spend longer fixing guests' login problems, measurably reducing desk productivity. How should this be treated?
options: As a dis-benefit to identify and manage
As a risk to record in the risk register
As an output to remove from scope
As an outcome to report as a benefit
C.why: A measurable decline resulting from an outcome, perceived as negative, is a dis-benefit; dis-benefits are identified and managed.

whyNot.1: It is already happening and measured, so it is not an uncertain future event.
whyNot.2: Lost productivity is not a product; it is a consequence of an outcome.
whyNot.3: It is a decline, so it cannot be reported as a benefit.

reteach.title: The gym membership
reteach.question: You buy a gym membership, start going three times a week, and lose 5 kg. Which part is the output, the outcome and the benefit?

blocks.body: The membership card is the output: the thing you got. Going three times a week is the outcome: your behaviour changed. Losing 5 kg is the benefit: a measurable improvement. Your goal of getting fit is like a business objective. If the gym trips cost you an hour of sleep each night, that measurable loss is a dis-benefit.

blocks.text: Buying the card does not make you fitter. Projects deliver outputs; outcomes and benefits depend on the outputs being used.

explain.body: An output is a deliverable (a product). A capability is the completed set of outputs needed to deliver an outcome.

options: The skills and experience held by the project team
The completed outputs needed for an outcome
A measurable improvement from an outcome
The result of change in behaviour
test.why: A capability is the completed set of project outputs required to deliver an outcome.

whyNot.0: Team skills are competencies, not a capability in the business case sense.

explain.body: The result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour and circumstances. Ask: are people now acting differently?

test.q: A project supplies tablets and software for recording patient observations. Which statement is an outcome?
options: Tablets and software are delivered
Observation errors fall by 20%
Nurses now record observations on tablets
The trust aims for measurably safer wards by 2027
test.why: Nurses changing how they record observations is the result of change in behaviour: an outcome.

whyNot.0: Delivering tablets and software is an output.
whyNot.1: A measurable 20% fall in errors is a benefit.
whyNot.3: A strategic aim like this is a business objective.

explain.body: Both are measurable and both result from outcomes. A benefit is an improvement seen as an advantage; a dis-benefit is a decline seen as negative.

test.q: Which statement about benefits is correct?
options: They are handed over as products at closure
They are agreed in each work package
They are the outputs the project delivers
They are measurable and result from outcomes
test.why: A benefit is the measurable improvement resulting from an outcome (manual 5.1).

whyNot.0: Products are outputs; benefits come from using them.
whyNot.1: Work packages cover products, with scope, cost and time tolerances, not benefits.
whyNot.2: Outputs are products; benefits result from outcomes.

explain.body: The measurable outcomes that show progress against the organization's strategy. The project's benefits should contribute to them.

test.q: What does a business objective demonstrate?
options: Progress against the approved stage plan
Progress against the organization's strategy
The quality of the products the project delivers
The status of the risks facing the project
test.why: A business objective is the measurable outcomes that demonstrate progress in relation to the organization's strategy.

whyNot.0: Progress against the stage plan is measured through the progress practice.
whyNot.2: Product quality is measured against quality specifications.
whyNot.3: Risk status is held in the risk register.
